title: VHF/UHF digital, APRS, EME and meteor scatter
blurb: Choose the right weak-signal mode for meteors or the Moon, and read APRS frames and digipeater paths.

E2D01.why: **MSK144** is the WSJT-X mode designed for meteor scatter's short bursts.
E2D01.trap: WSPR is a propagation beacon, APRS is tracking.

E2D02.why: A VHF contest exchange in FT8 or FT4 uses your **grid square** where a normal QSO sends the signal report.

E2D03.why: **Q65** is designed for EME. MSK144 is for meteors and WSPR is a beacon mode.

E2D04.why: Balloon trackers send position with **APRS**, which shows moving stations on a map in real time.

E2D05.why: JT65 **decodes signals with a very low signal-to-noise ratio**, even below the noise.
E2D05.trap: 65 is not its bandwidth or baud rate.

E2D06.why: EME uses **time-synchronous transmissions that alternate** between stations, since echoes are slow and weak.
E2D06.trap: Store-and-forward is a satellite mailbox technique.

E2D07.trap: PACTOR and AMTOR are HF modes.

E2D08.why: An APRS beacon is an **Unnumbered Information** frame: connectionless, with no acknowledgment.
E2D08.trap: Connect and Acknowledgement frames belong to connected sessions.

E2D09.why: JT65 sends **multitone AFSK**: many audio tones, one per symbol.

E2D10.why: WIDE3-1 means **three digipeater hops requested, one remaining**.

E2D11.why: APRS data is relayed by **packet digipeaters** that re-transmit what they hear.
E2D11.trap: APRS does not ride DMR or C4FM repeaters.
